messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels different—like the tide’s turning, but no one’s sure if it’s coming in or going out. The old guard’s still standing, but the cracks are showing, and the shopkeeper down the street just said what we’ve all been thinking. Keep your eyes open, but don’t rush—this could get messy before it gets better."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are cracking—even the generals are whispering it now. The air feels different, like the first warm day after winter, but we all know the thaw can bring floods. Keep your heads down, but trust your instincts—this isn’t just noise anymore."*"
Sender 3: "*"The ship’s drifting—even the ones at the wheel are whispering about it. The cracks are showing, but no one’s sure yet if they’ll hold or split wide open. Stay sharp, but keep your hands steady."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are cracking—quietly, but everyone’s heard the sound. The clinic’s stocking up, the elites are digging in, and the embassies are holding their breath. No one’s talking about *if*, just *when*… and whether the guns will stay in the armories when the time comes."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—less like the old quiet, more like the kind of stillness before a storm. The elites are hedging, the streets are loosening their tongues, and the banks are playing it safe, but the garbage isn’t getting picked up on time. Something’s shifting, but whether it’s the ground giving way or just the regime tightening its grip, I can’t say yet. Keep your eyes open, but don’t do anything that can’t be undone."*"
Sender 6: "*"Things feel like they’re sitting on a knife’s edge—no one’s saying it outright, but the whispers are getting louder, and the jokes are sharper. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing in the little things: late paychecks, half-working services, and the way even the most loyal-seeming people are quietly asking, ‘What if?’—not ‘if,’ but *when.* Stay sharp, but don’t do anything reckless. We’re not there yet, but we’re not *not* there either."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s admitting it yet. The usual signs are there, but quieter than you’d expect, almost like they’re waiting for something. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to draw attention."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the next move. The cracks are there, but the regime’s still holding the leash tight. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The right time will come."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, and no one’s pretending it isn’t. The usual rules don’t apply anymore, but we still need to move carefully. Let’s talk soon, but not here."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s admitting they feel it too. The usual signs are all there: the palace is quiet, the soldiers are new, and even the pharmacist is stocking up like he’s expecting a storm. We’re not imagining it—this isn’t just nerves, it’s the regime holding its breath. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The question isn’t *if*, but *how*."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are cracking—you can feel it in the way they’re scrambling. The song plays on every corner, the banks choke the taps, and the generals are watching each other instead of us. But don’t mistake panic for weakness—this could get uglier before it breaks. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and trust no sudden moves."*"
Sender 12: "*"The cracks are showing, but the walls are still standing—for now. The regime’s holding together with tape and promises, but the tape’s getting thinner, and the promises are starting to sound like excuses. Keep your eyes open, your ears sharp, and your supplies ready—just in case. And for the love of god, don’t trust the official line. Not even the quiet one."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s admitting they feel it too. The banks are whispering, the generals’ wives are packing, and the tea houses aren’t just complaining anymore. Something’s coming, but whether it’s a storm or just the calm before the regime locks down tighter, I don’t know. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we need to see which way the wind blows first."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels different—like the walls are shifting, but no one’s admitting they’re the ones moving them. The usual noise is quieter, the usual silences louder, and the only thing everyone agrees on is that something’s coming. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to trip over our own feet."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground is shifting under us, but no one’s pretending not to notice. The usual cracks are widening, and even the ones who used to whisper are talking louder. Stay sharp, but keep your head down—this isn’t over yet, and the worst thing we could do is assume we know how it ends."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are cracking—small things, but the kind that don’t go unnoticed. Two heads giving orders, no one correcting the record, and the streets breathing a little easier. But don’t mistake quiet for stillness. The embassies are holding their breath, and that’s never a good sign. Stay sharp, stay close, and for now—watch the gaps, not the guards."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the first tremors. The usual signs are there, but the regime’s playing it too quiet, and that’s what worries me."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different—like the moment before a storm when the birds go quiet. The usual signs are missing, but that’s the problem: the silence isn’t peace, it’s the sound of something holding its breath. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the ice cracking. The regime’s still barking, but the pack’s getting restless, and the handlers? They’re either losing their grip or playing a game we can’t see yet. Either way, we should all keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to move, but it might be the time to start counting who’s still standing."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s saying it out loud yet. The usual signs are there: the quiet ones are getting ready, the loud ones are too loud, and the middle? They’re just trying not to trip over their own feet. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels different—like the ground is shifting under us, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the first cracks. The usual players are either hiding, hedging, or moving pieces quietly, and even the streets feel like they’re holding their breath. Stay sharp, but don’t let the quiet fool you—this isn’t over, just… waiting."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the wind. The jokes are sharper, the orders slower, and the quiet in the streets isn’t just the weather. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are cracking—quietly, but fast. The banks are tightening, the streets are humming, and even the neighbors are acting like they’re staying. But the real question isn’t *if*, it’s *who*—and whether the old guard will fold before the whole thing collapses on them."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are cracking—even the usual suspects are stepping back, and the machine is sputtering. But no one knows if it’s the whole thing collapsing or just the facade. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are cracking—even the guards at the old barracks are new faces, and the merchant by the square packed up overnight. The game on Sunday had more people than I’ve seen in years, but the real talk isn’t on the pitch. My phone’s been acting strange, and the diplomats are suddenly ‘watching carefully.’ Something’s coming, but whether it’s a storm or a collapse, no one’s sure yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we need to see which way the wind blows first."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
